# Arachnids
Arachnids are a humanoid species with features resembling those of the common tarantula.
## Background
In the distant reaches of space, your ancestors were born on the shadowy exoplanet of Artabos: a rocky, lush planet rich in atmosphere and illuminated by dim lighting.
Although solitary, your kind were vastly intelligent, understanding the patterns of those you hunted and creating intricate traps that would snare even the wisest of prey. Other species on the planet of Artabos learned to fear your ancestors, viewing them as the boogeymen of the shadows. The arachnids did not feel pity, or most emotions for that matter: your kind were beyond such a vulnerability. All they knew was the cold, calculating strategies of survival.
The arachnids adapted to a secluded lifestyle, only interacting with others in dire situations. It wasn’t until other spacefaring species with advanced technology came across the planet of your ancestors that your kind learned there was far more to be analyzed… albeit with the aid of others. Your kind adapted fast to the methodology and machinery of other species, leading many to praise your kind for their sagacity and ability to acclimate to new environments. Nowadays your kind, despite your unnerving appearance, are revered for their tactical approaches to most situations.
## Unique Abilities
### Sericulture
- Arachnids can create Websilk at the cost of getting hungrier. They (and only they) can craft bundles of websilk into various items, from clothing and shields to entire walls.
## Diet
- They can eat raw meat without any ill effects. - They will get [color=#FFA500]poisoned[/color] by Theobromine (Chocolate, Tea, Coffee) and Allicin (Onion, Garlic).
## Benefits
- They have two additional Pocket slots in their inventory. - Their unarmed attacks deal [color=#ec3a3a]Piercing[/color] damage instead of Blunt.
## Drawbacks
- They [color=#FFA500]suffocate 50% faster.[/color] - their Blue Blood [color=#FFA500]can't be metabolised from Iron[/color], being based on Copper instead.
Despite their supposedly scary appearance, various species of spider share a fundamental kinship with Arachnids. Their bond draws them together and even allows them to converse in the same language.
